concept: Hidden indexes as a safe drop trial
summary: Source-anchored research for Hidden indexes as a safe drop trial. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: Because MongoDB maintains a hidden index, unhiding makes it immediately available for query planning without rebuilding it. Availability does not imply the planner will necessarily select it. (high confidence)

Use db.collection.hideIndex(indexName) and db.collection.unhideIndex(indexName) for the trial and rollback. Inspect db.collection.getIndexes() to verify hidden:true; the hidden field is omitted when the index is unhidden. (medium confidence)

Use db.collection.hideIndex("index_name") to hide an existing index and db.collection.unhideIndex("index_name") to restore planner eligibility; hideIndex is a mongosh wrapper around collMod with index.hidden. Verify the hidden flag with getIndexes(). (high confidence)

Hiding preserves unique constraints and TTL expiration. Consequently, a successful query-performance trial cannot establish the consequences of removing these enforcement or expiration behaviors. (high confidence)
Queries cannot use cursor.hint() to select a hidden index; operations that hint it return an exception. Check application hints before hiding a candidate index. (high confidence)

A hidden index is excluded from query-plan selection. Hiding an existing index therefore tests workload behavior without that access path while preserving a reversible alternative to dropping and rebuilding the index. (high confidence)

Hidden indexes remain updated by collection writes and consume disk space and memory. A hide trial evaluates plan selection; it does not measure the write-performance or storage savings of actually removing the index. (high confidence)

Choose an observation window that includes infrequent workloads. A 2024 practitioner thread described jobs that used candidate indexes only once every three months, illustrating why a short quiet trial can miss a dependency. (low confidence)

As a concrete tooling example, mdbkit prints reversible hideIndex commands for index candidates and warns that an index used monthly can look unused after a week of observation. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

Before hiding, compare query behavior with the index available; then hide it and compare query performance and plans. If performance regresses, unhide it. This is a reversible experiment that can still expose the application to degraded query performance during the trial. (high confidence)

Changing an index from visible to hidden resets its $indexStats. Capture usage evidence before starting the trial; do not treat post-hide statistics as an uninterrupted historical baseline. (high confidence)
MongoDB does not allow hiding the _id index. (high confidence)
